explanations.e: The internal inguinal ring is an opening in the transversalis fascia, forming the posterior wall at this site.
The lateral pterygoid attaches to the articular disc and capsule of the temporomandibular joint.
The glomerulus is a tuft of fenestrated capillaries enclosed by Bowman's capsule.
The left 6th aortic arch forms the left pulmonary artery and, via its distal part, the ductus arteriosus.
The urachus becomes the median umbilical ligament after obliteration.
The common fibular nerve is vulnerable around the neck of the fibula; its deep fibular branch supplies dorsiflexors.
The greater auricular nerve supplies sensation over the skin around the angle of the mandible and parotid region, including the area below the ear lobule.
